title: About GeoUnpack
description: Who makes GeoUnpack, why it exists, how it converts Esri files locally in your browser, what it can't do yet, and how to get in touch.
html:
GeoUnpack is a small independent tool made by Jiayi, an independent developer based in Canada. It exists because people regularly receive ArcGIS layer packages, map packages and file geodatabases without having an ArcGIS licence, and the free workarounds (renaming files, installing QGIS, using command-line GDAL) are not obvious to everyone.

How it works

When you drop a file, your browser unpacks it with 7-Zip and reads it with the open-source GDAL library, both compiled to WebAssembly. The conversion runs on your own computer. Your files are never uploaded, and there is no account or server-side storage.

What it can and can't do

  • Opens .lpk, .lpkx, .mpk, .mpkx and zipped .gdb files.
  • Exports vector layers and tables to Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KML and CSV.
  • Not supported yet: raster, tile and scene packages, symbology and labels, files over 150 MB.

Always keep your original file and check converted data before relying on it.

Independence

GeoUnpack is not affiliated with or endorsed by Esri. It uses only open-source libraries, listed on the licenses page.

Contact

Found a file that doesn't convert, or have a suggestion? Email hello@geounpack.com. Sample files that fail (if you are allowed to share them) help the most.

title: Privacy
description: GeoUnpack does not upload or store your files.
html:
Your files never leave your computer. When you open a file, it is read by code running in your browser. Nothing about the file's content is sent to us or to anyone else.

The map preview loads background map tiles from OpenStreetMap's tile servers; those requests contain only the map area being displayed, not your data.

We use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which counts page views without cookies and without tracking you across sites.

If you buy a licence in the future, payment is handled by our payment provider; we receive your email address and the purchase details only.

title: Open-source licenses
html:
GeoUnpack is built on these open-source projects. Thank you to their authors.

  • gdal3.js (GDAL compiled to WebAssembly): LGPL-2.1-or-later. GDAL itself is MIT/X licensed; bundled dependencies carry their own licenses. The unmodified library files are loaded from the jsDelivr CDN (npm package gdal3.js@2.8.1); source code is available at the link above.
  • 7z-wasm (7-Zip compiled to WebAssembly): 7-Zip is licensed under the GNU LGPL with the unRAR restriction. Source: 7-zip.org.
  • Leaflet: BSD-2-Clause.
  • fflate: MIT.
  • Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
